plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy: bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth, while bidding lower reduces my chances of winning profitable auctions without changing what I'd pay if I win. Since my value is $24, I will bid exactly $24 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the weakly dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value adds no benefit and only risks overpaying if I'm the highest. Bidding below my value only risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $16 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since the price I pay is determined by the second-highest bid (not my own bid), bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds what others bid) and never overpay (since I'd only pay the second-highest bid, which would be less than my value if I win). Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I'm forced to pay close to my bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $24, so I'll bid exactly that.
